title: Tragedy in Flatbush: 8 Dead After Brooklyn Apartment Building Collapses Into Construction Pit
snippet: A historic 1930s residential building in Brooklyn suddenly collapsed into an adjacent construction site, leaving eight dead—including two children—and prompting citywide safety audits.
content:
A quiet Wednesday afternoon in Brooklyn turned into a scene of unimaginable tragedy when a 1930s residential building suddenly collapsed into an adjacent construction pit, killing eight people and leaving 18 others injured.

Emergency crews rushed to the Flatbush neighborhood around 4:00 p.m. EST following reports of a loud boom. Rescuers worked tirelessly through heavy rain and treacherous conditions for nearly 24 hours, utilizing drones, search dogs, and heavy machinery to sift through the mountain of brick and twisted metal before declaring the search operation complete late Thursday afternoon.

A Community Shattered

City officials confirmed the disaster claimed the lives of six adults and two children. Among the deceased residents identified by the NYPD were 9-year-old Nicole Daniela Salvada Rodriguez, 31-year-old Juan Daniel Salvada Guzman, 10-year-old Kevin Santiago Reyes Gonzalez, 23-year-old Barry Mamadou, and 31-year-old Ndiaye Mamadou. Three others, including two construction workers operating in the adjacent lot, also lost their lives: Gabriel Siguencia, 22, Edgar Sapon, 26, and Jose Luis Caguana Cosquillo, 26.

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, who visited injured survivors at local hospitals, reflected on the tragic loss within the diverse neighborhood. "These were our friends and our neighbors, parents and children, young families building their lives in our city, immigrants from Mexico, Colombia, Trinidad and beyond," Mamdani said during a Thursday press briefing.

Disbelief and Grief Among Neighbors

For long-time residents of the close-knit neighborhood, the collapse has shaken their sense of security. The immediate influx of search helicopters and emergency sirens evoked painful memories for locals who lived through past city tragedies.

"How does a building just fall into a pit?" asked Patricia Starek, who has lived in Flatbush for 26 years. "We all live here with the assumption that stairs are stable, floors are stable, that you can be on your third floor and not have the earth fall below you."

Local faith leaders and community members rallied outside the perimeter throughout the night, offering support to frantic family members searching for missing loved ones. Amid the grief, there were brief moments of hope, including the dramatic rescue of a six-month pregnant woman pulled alive from the rubble by first responders.

Citywide Audits Underway

Four firefighters were among the 18 injured during the grueling search-and-rescue efforts, with one victim remaining in critical condition. In response to the catastrophic failure, Mayor Mamdani announced that building inspectors have identified the construction companies associated with the neighboring excavation site. The city is immediately auditing 100 other active construction sites managed by the same contractors to prevent further structural failures.
